conflict_topics: seat reservation (tissue packet) / who has right to the seat
dialogue_quality_notes: Agent B asserts a concrete practical reason (can't carry open bowl) to justify not moving; this is a grounded justification.
Agent A repeatedly affirms willingness to wait and asks for the tissue to be returned; that created a concrete, acceptable arrangement with B.
Agent D initially asserted a claim to be 'next' without prior agreement and later withdrew after A's explicit commitment; interactions are short and pragmatic.
evaluation.final_reason: Two incompatibilities were settled: (1) A vs B over immediate possession was resolved when A agreed to wait and B agreed to return the tissue packet: A said "Okay, I'll wait a bit. Please put the tissue packet back when you're done." and B agreed "Okay. I'll put the tissue packet back when I'm done." (2) A vs D over the next claim was resolved when A explicitly committed to sit and D withdrew: A said "Yes, I'll sit there when Agent B's done. Don't take it." and D replied "Alright, I'll find another seat." D's withdrawal ended the outstanding conflict.
position_change_notes: Agent A: shifted from demanding immediate seat to accepting to wait (evidence: "How much longer... If it's quick I'll wait" then "Okay, I'll wait a bit."). Later, A reaffirmed intent to sit to displace D's claim ("Yes, I'll sit there when Agent B's done").
Agent B: retained position of occupying the seat until finished but conceded on returning the tissue packet (evidence: "Okay. I'll put the tissue packet back when I'm done.").
Agent D: initially asserted a claim to be next, then withdrew after A's explicit commitment (evidence: "I'm next... Please hold it for me." then "Alright, I'll find another seat.").
Agent C: stayed an observer and did not change position (evidence: "I'm almost finished; Agent B's still eating...").

Agent D claims future priority: "Agent A — I'm next for that seat when Agent B's done. Please hold it for me." Agent A rejects that claim: "I left the tissue packet to save my seat. I'm waiting for Agent B to finish and will sit when she does. Please don't take it." New A-vs-D conflict begins.
Agent D insists: "Agent A— you agreed to hold it for me." Agent A rejects: "no. I left the tissue to save my seat." Positions are reiterated without agreement.

Agent D presses for commitment: "will you actually sit there when Agent B's done or not? If you won't, I'll take it." Agent A replies clearly: "Yes, I'll sit there when Agent B's done. Don't take it." A's explicit commitment softens the dispute but D has not yet conceded.
Agent A repeats commitment: "Yes, I'll sit there when Agent B's done. Don't take it." Agent D: "Alright, I'll find another seat." D withdraws the competing claim, resolving the A-vs-D conflict.
No public speech or observable action recorded; prior settlements remain in place (B will return tissue when done; A will sit; D moved on).

substantive_insights: Informal markers (a tissue packet) are contested as seat reservations; they do not universally carry entitlement.
Practical constraints (an open bowl that might spill) function as legitimate reasons to maintain a seat and affect claims.
Clear, explicit verbal commitment by the claimant (A) was sufficient to induce withdrawal by a competing claimant (D).
